info.name: Voice Agent - D3 money flow
info.description:
Wallet, Stripe and the config cache (spec §5, §13.7, §13.10, §14; admin §5).

## Before the first run

1. `pnpm infra:up && pnpm db:deploy && pnpm db:seed`, then start the API on :4000.
2. Get a customer JWT. In this collection's **Authorization** tab, Type is Bearer with `{{token}}`. Fill `token` in the environment either from Postman's own OAuth 2.0 helper or from the Auth0 API Test tab.

   OAuth 2.0 helper settings (customer tenant, SPA app `Voice Agent`):
   - Grant type: Authorization Code (With PKCE)
   - Auth URL: `https://dev-tpj0dmu6yauk2360.us.auth0.com/authorize`
   - Access Token URL: `https://dev-tpj0dmu6yauk2360.us.auth0.com/oauth/token`
   - Client ID: `l0UZ5TKdAcHETAzg0swJFIVeFftfJBd3`, no secret
   - Callback URL: `https://oauth.pstmn.io/v1/callback` (add it to the app's Allowed Callback URLs)
   - Scope: `openid profile email`
   - Advanced → Auth request params: `audience` = `https://api.metacognixion.com`

3. Link the token to a local account and get a workspace id — the users upsert lands with D5, so until then:

   ```sh
   cd backend/api
   pnpm exec dotenv -e ../../.env -- tsx scripts/dev-link-user.ts "<token>"
   ```

   Put its `workspace_id` into the `workspace_id` environment variable.

4. Copy `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` from `.env` into `stripe_webhook_secret`. Folder E signs its own payloads with it, so the Stripe CLI is optional.

## Running it

Collection Runner, top to bottom. Folders A–C read, D creates purchases, E fires signed webhooks, F proves the credits landed and that the replay changed nothing.

## Not in here

Metering (`duration_s → credits`) has no HTTP route until D4 wires the Retell `call_ended` handler. It is covered by `backend/api/src/modules/calls/metering.test.ts` against the real D2 payloads, and the ledger side by `backend/api/test/wallet.e2e.test.ts`.

item.name: A. Public config — no token needed
item.description: `GET /pricing` is public because W7 renders the pack cards before anyone signs in. Both routes are served from Redis with a 60 s TTL; a second call returns the same `version` without touching Postgres.

request.description: Liveness. Run this first — everything below assumes the API is up on :4000.
The current pricing_configs version, projected to what a customer may see. Hidden packs and the staff-only wallet policy fields (max first purchase, MFA threshold) are stripped here, not in the UI.

exec: pm.test('a version is in effect', () => pm.expect(b.version).to.be.at.least(1));
pm.test('the four §5.2 packs are on sale', () => pm.expect(b.packs.map(p => p.id)).to.include.members(['starter','growth','scale','pro']));

pm.test('staff-only policy fields are not leaked', () => { pm.expect(b.wallet_policy).to.not.have.property('mfa_required_above_balance'); pm.expect(b.wallet_policy).to.not.have.property('max_first_purchase_cents_without_review'); });

request.description: Region filter. A pack with a `regions` list is only offered in those countries; a pack with an empty list is offered everywhere, which is every pack in the seeded v1 config.

exec: pm.test('same config version as the unfiltered read', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().version).to.be.at.least(1));

item.name: B. Flags, caps and the auth boundary
item.description: `GET /flags` is per workspace: plan gates ∘ tenant overrides ∘ feature flags, plus the four SA12 kill switches (admin §5.3). The three negative requests are the tenancy boundary from ADR 0006.

request.description: Everything the portal branches on for this workspace.

exec: pm.test('carries the config version that produced it', () => pm.expect(b.config_version).to.be.at.least(1));
pm.test('all four kill switches are reported', () => pm.expect(Object.keys(b.kill_switches).sort()).to.eql(['pause_generation','pause_purchases','pause_web_tests','reject_inbound']));
pm.test('no kill switch is on', () => pm.expect(Object.values(b.kill_switches).every(v => v === false)).to.be.true);

request.description: Routes are authenticated by default; only @Public() opts out. A new controller added on a busy day is protected, not exposed.
Every workspace-scoped route needs X-Workspace-Id (§16). WorkspaceGuard answers before anything reads the database.
A workspace you are not a member of answers the same way as one that does not exist, so the route cannot be used to probe for valid ids.

item.name: C. Wallet reads
item.description: Balance, lots and the append-only ledger (D5 screen, §16). These run inside withWorkspace(), so RLS is the second guard behind the membership check.

request.description: The D5 balance card. `balance` is Σ credit_ledger.delta to 2 dp; the read also refreshes bal:{ws} so the inbound path (D4) agrees with what the customer just saw.

exec: pm.test('reports the plan tier and caps', () => { pm.expect(b).to.have.property('plan_tier'); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('concurrency_cap'); });

request.description: Every lot, soonest expiry first — the order FIFO consumption follows (§5.4).

exec: pm.test('sorted by expiry', () => { const d = lots.map(l => l.expires_at); pm.expect(d).to.eql([...d].sort()); });

request.description: Cursor pagination (§16). The cursor is an opaque keyset position, so rows inserted while the customer reads are never duplicated or skipped.

exec: pm.test('newest first', () => { const t = b.items.map(i => i.created_at); pm.expect(t).to.eql([...t].sort().reverse()); });
pm.test('every row carries a running balance', () => b.items.forEach(i => pm.expect(i.balance_after).to.be.a('number')));

request.description: Feeds the previous response's next_cursor back in. Skips itself when page 1 was the last page, so a young workspace does not show a red failure here.

exec: console.log('Page 1 returned next_cursor: null — this workspace has one page of ledger. Skipping.');
pm.test('skipped — the ledger fits on one page', () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

request.description: The D5 ledger filter. Reasons are the §15 enum: trial, purchase, call, rental, kb, adjustment, expiry, refund, topup.

exec: pm.test('only purchase rows come back', () => pm.response.json().items.forEach(i => pm.expect(i.reason).to.eql('purchase')));

request.description: A cursor is opaque so clients cannot forge one into an offset. A malformed one is refused rather than silently treated as page 1.

item.name: D. Checkout (§13.7)
item.description: Creates a pending `purchases` row and a real Stripe Checkout Session with client_reference_id = purchase_id, our ids in metadata, and setup_future_usage only when auto top-up was asked for. No credits move here — the webhook in folder E does that.

request.description: Open `checkout_url` in a browser and pay with 4242 4242 4242 4242 for the real path (needs `stripe listen` running), or just run folder E to fire the webhook yourself. Doing both is safe: whichever arrives second finds the purchase already paid and credits nothing. Needs owner or admin, plus a verified email.

exec: console.warn('Verify your Auth0 email, or use a token that carries the https://portal/email_verified claim.');

item.name: 2. POST /wallet/checkout — second one, to expire later

request.description: A pending purchase folder E abandons with a checkout.session.expired event.
Packs come from the current pricing config, never from code. An id that is not in it, is inactive, or is hidden (staff-assignable only) is refused.
Bodies are validated by the shared zod schema, and the §16 envelope carries per-field messages.

item.name: E. Stripe webhook (§13.10)
item.description:
The signature is computed in each request's Pre-request Script exactly the way Stripe computes it, so these exercise the real verification path against request.rawBody — no mocking, and no Stripe CLI needed. Set `stripe_webhook_secret` in the environment first.

Run them in order: unsigned → tampered → signed completed → replay → expired.

request.description: No stripe-signature header at all. Nothing is stored: the event never gets past verification.
A well-formed header signed with the wrong key. Also catches a stale timestamp — Stripe's tolerance is 5 minutes and we keep it.
The money moment. Marks the purchase paid, creates a 12-month credit lot, writes one positive ledger row and recomputes the plan tier — all in one locked transaction.

exec: // Signs the body exactly the way Stripe does: HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<raw body>`
// keyed with the endpoint's signing secret, sent as `t=<ts>,v1=<hex>`. The API verifies it
// against request.rawBody, so the bytes signed here and the bytes sent must be identical —
// which is why the body is nothing but {{stripe_payload}}.
if (!secret) { throw new Error('Set stripe_webhook_secret in the environment — copy STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET from .env, or run `stripe listen --print-secret`.'); }
// A replay must carry the SAME event id, so it is generated once and remembered.
if (!eventId || pm.variables.get('fresh_event') === 'true') { eventId = 'evt_pm_' + hex(24); pm.environment.set('stripe_event_id', eventId); }
if (!purchaseId) { throw new Error('No purchase id yet — run the checkout request in folder D first.'); }
console.log('event id kept for the replay:', pm.environment.get('stripe_event_id'));

item.name: 4. The same event again → 204, no second credit

request.description: Re-signs a fresh body under the SAME event id, which is what Stripe does when it retries. The unique key on webhook_events (provider, external_id, event_type) turns it into a 204 no-op. This is the D3 exit check: a duplicate webhook must not create duplicate credits.

if (!purchaseId) { throw new Error('No purchase id yet — run the checkout request in folder D first.'); }

request.description: Abandons the second pending purchase from folder D. A purchase that is already paid is left alone.

item.name: F. Verify the money landed
item.description: Run after folder E. Proves the webhook moved exactly one pack of credits into the wallet and left a readable trail.

item.name: 1. GET /wallet — balance rose by one Growth pack

request.description: Compares against the balance folder C recorded before the purchase.

exec: pm.test('plan tier is at least growth', () => pm.expect(['growth','scale','pro','volume']).to.include(pm.response.json().plan_tier));
pm.test('the pack size is remembered for the low-balance thresholds', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().last_pack_credits).to.be.a('number'));

item.name: 2. GET /wallet/ledger — exactly one row for this purchase

request.description: The replay in E4 must not appear here. One purchase, one row, forever.

exec: pm.test('exactly one ledger row for the purchase', () => pm.expect(rows.length).to.eql(1));

request.description: The lot the purchase created. FIFO will burn whatever expires before it first.

exec: pm.test('the lot exists and is untouched', () => { pm.expect(lot, 'no lot of ' + want + ' credits').to.exist; pm.expect(lot.credits_remaining).to.eql(want); });
pm.test('it expires in about 12 months (§5.4)', () => { const months = (new Date(lot.expires_at) - Date.now()) / (30.4 * 86400000); pm.expect(months).to.be.within(11.4, 12.6); });
